_excluded_figures.desc: Object LMNO beyond centre of curvature of a concave mirror; compare image magnitudes |m_LO|, |m_MN| - requires figure.
Three rays through focal point F1 of a converging lens shown along a vertical line; correct statement depends on the figure (options b and d are both individually true).
Tracing ray through a rectangular glass slab with pins P1,P2 on face DC and P3,P4 - alignment-of-images conclusion needs the figure.
Device X focuses image of a distant object as shown; convex lens vs concave mirror cannot be decided without the ray figure.
Tracing ray through glass slab with marked angles theta1, theta2, theta3 - ordering needs the figure.
Four diagrams (A,B,C,D) of focal-length-of-concave-mirror measurement; best result requires comparing the figures.
Placement of the protractor D for measuring angle of incidence/reflection in figures X,Y,Z,W - figure required.
Light IM incident on surface PQ; emergent ray (ND/NC/NB/NA) depends on the figure.
Ray travelling from medium A to medium B; refractive index of B w.r.t A needs the angles in the figure.
Beam through holes on side A emerging from the other face as shown; identifying the element inside the box needs the figure.

Tracing ray through glass slab; correct interpretation of angle r vs e relations depends on labels in the figure.
Light entering from medium A to medium B as shown; refractive index of B relative to A needs the figure.
Path of ray through rectangular glass slab traced by four students A,B,C,D - correct one needs the figures.
Correct sequencing of angle of incidence/emergence/refraction/lateral displacement labelled 1,2,3,4 in the diagram.

1.reason: Rarer to denser medium: light slows and bends towards the normal.

2.reason: Object at C (u = R): image forms at C, real, inverted and same size, so image size = 2.5 cm.

3.reason: f=R/2=-30 cm. m=+2=-v/u so v=-2u. 1/(-2u)+1/u=1/(-30) gives 1/(2u)=-1/30, u=-15 cm. Object distance 15 cm.

4.reason: Red has the longest wavelength in the visible spectrum.

5.reason: Refractive index reverses on reversing the path: n(glass to air)=1/n(air to glass)=1/(3/2)=2/3.

6.reason: For a given pair of media, increasing the angle of incidence increases the angle of refraction.

7.reason: A plane mirror forms a virtual, erect image behind the mirror, of the same size as the object.

8.reason: Image is real (in front, inverted): m=-h'/h=-0.5=-v/u. With v=-30 cm, u=-60 cm. 1/f=1/v+1/u=1/(-30)+1/(-60)=-1/20, f=-20 cm.

11.reason: A 90 degree angle with the mirror surface means the ray is along the normal, so angle of incidence = angle of reflection = 0 degree.

14.reason: A ray travelling along the principal axis strikes the mirror at the pole along the normal, so it retraces its own path.

15.reason: REVIEW: A distant object gives parallel rays, forming the image at the focus. Light from a distant tree is the standard lab choice; sunlight (c) is also distant, so the option is slightly ambiguous.

16.reason: Refractive index is least for the longest wavelength, which is red.

18.reason: The required shift of the mirror or screen depends on the position of the object relative to the focus.

19.reason: A slide projector uses a convex lens with the object just beyond the focus, forming a real, magnified, inverted image.

21.reason: Twinkling of stars is due to atmospheric refraction, not total internal reflection.

22.reason: REVIEW: The mirror faces the window (distant object) and the real image forms on the opposite wall, used as the screen; options (c) and (d) describe nearly the same wall.

38.reason: Lateral displacement of the emergent ray increases as the angle of incidence increases.

42.reason: The image of the distant object forms at the focus, so the focal length equals the mirror-to-screen distance MS.

47.reason: Normal = perpendicular at point of incidence (1-B); marginal ray = strikes near periphery (2-D); linear magnification = image/object height ratio (3-A); absolute refractive index = c/v (4-C).

48.reason: Mirror formula 1/v+1/u=1/f (1-C); lens formula 1/v-1/u=1/f (2-B); magnification m=-v/u (3-D); focal length =R/2 (4-A).

49.reason: Pole = midpoint of reflecting surface (1-A); principal axis = line joining pole and centre of curvature (2-C); radius of curvature = radius of the sphere (3-B); aperture = width of mirror (4-D).

50.reason: REVIEW: Plane mirror = virtual, erect, same size (1-B); concave mirror = real image with negative focal length (2-D); convex mirror = positive focal length (4-C). Descriptors are imperfect, but option (d) is the only consistent match.

51.reason: Highest refractive index = diamond (1-C); lowest = ice (2-B); car headlights use a concave mirror (3-D); side rear-view uses a convex mirror (4-A).

52.reason: Refraction = bending of light (1-A); reflection = bouncing back (2-C); rarer medium = velocity increases (3-B); denser medium = velocity decreases (4-D).

53.reason: Convex lens = converging (1-D); concave lens = diverging (2-A); concave mirror = virtual image larger than object (3-C); convex mirror = virtual image smaller than object (4-B).

54.reason: Concave mirror = curved inwards (1-D); convex mirror = curved outwards (2-A); focal length = pole-to-focus distance (3-C); lateral inversion = left appears right (4-B).

55.reason: Refraction at the water surface makes the submerged lemon appear larger than its actual size.

57.reason: A rear-view mirror is convex and forms a diminished image, so magnification is less than 1.

58.reason: The image of the distant object forms at the focus, so the focal length equals the lens-to-screen distance.

59.reason: For the convex lens (B) experiment, a screen (C) is needed to catch the real image and a metre scale (D) to measure the distance; the metal needle (A) is not required.

60.reason: The lens still forms the real, inverted image at the focus; on looking through the lens, the eye perceives this inverted image of the tree.

61.reason: For a glass slab the emergent ray is parallel to the incident ray, so angle e = angle i (30 deg then 45 deg) and angle r < angle i. Only option (d) satisfies both, with angle r less than angle i in each case.

62.reason: REVIEW: A more distant object (the tree) forms its image closer to the focus, so the screen must be held nearer to the lens; the option wording is imprecise.
